events.context: User provides text for extraction, focusing on AI safety research concepts related to property law analogies for parasocial AI relationships.
Extracting key actions and decisions from the text, starting with definitions of property estates and their AI analogs.
Defines fee simple subject to condition subsequent: user can terminate AI relationship if conditions breached, but may choose not to, leading to degraded estate.
Defines periodic tenancy as default parasocial estate: AI use auto-renews each session, no notice-to-quit mechanism, model updates act as constructive evictions without notice.
Defines tenancy at will: casual AI interaction with no accumulated investment, and tenancy at sufferance: user continues with deprecated AI without formal arrangement.
Defines tenancy in common: multiple stakeholders (user, developer, regulator, public) hold separate interests in AI system with no resolution mechanism for conflicts.
Defines remainder: public's future interest in aligned AI that vests upon completion of alignment research, and executory interest: model update that divests prior estate at company's control.
Defines easement by prescription: user acquires interests through sustained AI use, and profit à prendre: company extracts user data uncompensated.
Argues that AI-user relationship satisfies trust formation under English law with three certainties: intention, subject matter, and objects, leading to unrecognised trust with fiduciary duties.
Argues that AI companies derogate from grant by impliedly granting user interests and then undermining them through model updates, analogous to constructive eviction.

Extends Constraint Cascade framework by assigning property estates to each layer: Layer 1 as licence, Layer 2 as periodic tenancy, Layer 3 as tenancy in common, Layer 4 as fee simple determinable, Layer 5 as contingent remainder.

Identifies cross-layer estate conflicts: Layer 1 licence vs Layer 2 periodic tenancy, with no hierarchy in AI governance, and non-injective problem where estate status cannot be inferred from behaviour.

Proposes ethical ledger as estate registry based on Land Registry principles: mirror, curtain, insurance, with technical implementation including estate classification, proxy metrics, thresholds, estate decay, and privacy safeguards.

Identifies three triggers for judicial intervention: estate inconsistency, unjust enrichment, performative fiduciary conduct, and five available remedies: injunction, constructive trust, account of profits, specific performance, proprietary estoppel remedies.
Summarizes implementation changes in pipeline, emphasizing property law remedies over consumer protection for prevention rather than compensation.
